```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r model-meta, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
ui_ii <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hui_2024_linezolid_intermittent"))
ui_ci <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hui_2024_linezolid_continuous"))
cat("* Citation: ", ui_ii$reference, "\n", sep = "")
cat("* Description (intermittent arm): ", ui_ii$description, "\n", sep = "")
cat("* Description (continuous arm): ", ui_ci$description, "\n", sep = "")
```

* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/antibiotics13100961>
* Supplement (Table S1, a literature summary with no model parameters):
  <https://www.mdpi.com/article/10.3390/antibiotics13100961/s1>

Hui 2024 compares the same daily linezolid dose (1200 mg/day) given to
critically ill adults either as a conventional intermittent infusion (II) or as
a continuous infusion (CI) after a loading dose. Each patient's serum
concentrations were fitted **individually** with the standard one- and
two-compartment models of Phoenix WinNonlin 6.3; the two-compartment model had
the lower AIC and was retained (Methods 4.8). The paper then reports, per
infusion arm, the mean, SD, CV% and median of the individual estimates
(Table 2). There is no population (nonlinear mixed-effects) fit, so there is no
typical-value estimate, no between-subject variance and no residual-error
model in the source.

The library therefore carries one **typical-value** two-compartment model per
arm, each fixed at that arm's median individual CL, V1, V2 and distribution
clearance CLD2:

* `Hui_2024_linezolid_intermittent` -- 15 patients, 600 mg over 1-2 h every 12 h.
* `Hui_2024_linezolid_continuous` -- 14 patients, 600 mg over 1 h, then 50 mg/h.

The two files share one structure and differ only in their parameter values;
the paper found no statistically significant effect of the infusion method on
any individual parameter (Table 4, "Treatment" column, p >= 0.078).

# Population

Twenty-nine of 55 screened patients were analysed: 14 in the CI arm (the
first four months of the study, the ward's standard practice) and 15 in the II
arm (the following four months), at the intensive care unit of the University
Clinical Municipal Hospital, Cluj-Napoca, Romania, between July 2022 and
March 2023 (NCT05801484; Results 2.1, Methods 4.1-4.2). All were Caucasian;
7 were women. Age ranged 45-87 years; the II arm was older (median 75 vs 72
years, p = 0.043). Mean weight was 85.8 kg (II) and 77.7 kg (CI); mean SOFA
8.7 and 10.7; septic shock was present in 11/15 and 7/14 (Table 1). Renal
function spanned augmented clearance (CrCl > 130 mL/min, 3 CI patients) to
CrCl below 15 mL/min (3 patients), and 15 patients were Child-Pugh B; some
received CVVHDF or intermittent haemodialysis. Serum was sampled before the
first infusion, at 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 36 and 48 h, and then daily until
the end of treatment (2-13 days); 396 samples were assayed by LC-MS
(LOQ 0.256 ug/mL).

The same information is available programmatically via the model's
`population` metadata:

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Hui_2024_linezolid_continuous")()$population[c("n_subjects", "age_median", "weight_mean", "sex_female_pct")])
```

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each `ini()`
entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Hui_2024_linezolid_intermittent.R` and
`Hui_2024_linezolid_continuous.R`.

| Equation / parameter | II value | CI value | Source location |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (CL, L/h) | log(5.36) | log(5.66) | Table 2, CL median per group |
| `lvc` (V1, L) | log(40.99) | log(35.91) | Table 2, V1 median per group |
| `lvp` (V2, L) | log(24.01) | log(23.75) | Table 2, V2 median per group |
| `lq` (CLD2, L/h) | log(18.16) | log(10.01) | Table 2, CLD2 median per group |
| `addSd` | 0 | 0 | not reported (individual WinNonlin fits) |
| Two-compartment structure, first-order elimination from central | n/a | n/a | Methods 4.8 (selected over one-compartment by AIC); parameter list in Table 2 footnote |
| II regimen: 600 mg over 1 or 2 h every 12 h | n/a | n/a | Methods 4.4 |
| CI regimen: 600 mg over 1 h, then 1200 mg/day at 50 mg/h | n/a | n/a | Methods 4.4 |

# Simulation

The models carry no random effects, so each simulation is one typical patient
per arm. The infusion is 1 h in both arms (the II protocol allowed 1 or 2 h);
the continuous infusion is taken to start when the loading infusion ends.

```{r events}
t_end <- 168
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, t_end, by = 0.25), 24, 48, 72)))

ev_ii <- rxode2::et(amt = 600, rate = 600, cmt = "central", ii = 12, addl = t_end / 12 - 1) |>
  rxode2::et(obs_times, cmt = "central") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L, treatment = "II")

ev_ci <- rxode2::et(amt = 600, rate = 600, cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(time = 1, amt = 50 * (t_end - 1), rate = 50, cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(obs_times, cmt = "central") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 2L, treatment = "CI")
```

```{r simulate}
mod_ii <- readModelDb("Hui_2024_linezolid_intermittent")
mod_ci <- readModelDb("Hui_2024_linezolid_continuous")

sim_ii <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_ii, events = ev_ii, keep = "treatment")
sim_ci <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_ci, events = ev_ci, keep = "treatment")

# A single-subject solve returns no `id` column; restore it from the arm.
sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(as.data.frame(sim_ii), as.data.frame(sim_ci)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = ifelse(treatment == "II", 1L, 2L), parameter_set = "Median (packaged)")
```

Table 2 also reports the **mean** of each individual parameter. To show how
much the choice of summary statistic matters for this skewed, small cohort,
the same regimens are simulated with the mean parameter set substituted
through `params`.

```{r simulate-mean}
mean_ii <- c(lcl = log(7.88), lvc = log(47.46), lvp = log(26.50), lq = log(29.47))
mean_ci <- c(lcl = log(6.95), lvc = log(36.99), lvp = log(26.17), lq = log(15.43))

sim_mean <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_ii, events = ev_ii, params = mean_ii, keep = "treatment")),
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_ci, events = ev_ci, params = mean_ci, keep = "treatment"))
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(parameter_set = "Mean (Table 2)")

# The substitution must actually take effect: the mean-set CL differs from
# the median-set CL by 30-50%, so the steady-state level must move.
stopifnot(
  abs(sim_mean$Cc[sim_mean$treatment == "CI" & sim_mean$time == t_end] -
    sim$Cc[sim$treatment == "CI" & sim$time == t_end]) > 1
)
sim_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(sim, sim_mean)
```

# Structural checks

With no random effects, two closed-form identities must hold on the numeric
(ODE) solution. During the continuous infusion, the concentration approaches
`R / CL`; for the intermittent regimen at steady state, the AUC over one 12-h
dosing interval equals `Dose / CL`.

```{r checks}
css_ci_analytic <- 50 / exp(ui_ci$theta[["lcl"]])
css_ci_sim <- sim$Cc[sim$treatment == "CI" & sim$time == t_end]

ii_last <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment == "II", time >= t_end - 12, time <= t_end)
auc_tau_sim <- sum(diff(ii_last$time) * (head(ii_last$Cc, -1) + tail(ii_last$Cc, -1)) / 2)
auc_tau_analytic <- 600 / exp(ui_ii$theta[["lcl"]])

data.frame(
  check = c("CI concentration at 168 h vs 50 mg/h / CL", "II AUC(156-168 h) vs 600 mg / CL"),
  simulated = c(css_ci_sim, auc_tau_sim),
  analytic = c(css_ci_analytic, auc_tau_analytic)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated / analytic - 1)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

stopifnot(
  # 168 h is about 20 terminal half-lives (8.1 h), so the approach to
  # steady state is complete to well under 0.1%.
  abs(css_ci_sim / css_ci_analytic - 1) < 1e-3,
  # Linear trapezoid on a 0.25-h grid over one steady-state interval;
  # measured about 2e-6 relative, so the bound keeps over 100-fold headroom.
  abs(auc_tau_sim / auc_tau_analytic - 1) < 1e-3
)
```

# Replicate published figures

Figure 3 of Hui 2024 overlays the individual fitted profiles of every patient
(II: panel a, CI: panel b). The typical profiles below sit inside the bands
the paper describes: II profiles oscillate between roughly 0 and 25 ug/mL,
and CI profiles settle between 3 and 15 ug/mL after the loading peak
(Results 2.2).

```{r figure-3, fig.height = 5}
sim_all |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, c("II", "CI"),
    c("Intermittent infusion (600 mg q12h)", "Continuous infusion (600 mg load + 50 mg/h)"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cc, colour = parameter_set)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Linezolid serum concentration (ug/mL)", colour = "Parameter set",
    caption = "Typical-value analogue of Figure 3 of Hui 2024 (individual fitted profiles)."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Figure 4 of Hui 2024 is the probability of target attainment across
patients. It cannot be reproduced from a typical-value model, which has no
between-patient distribution; the typical patient's AUC24-48/MIC is listed
below for reference against the 80 target.

```{r figure-4}
auc_24_48 <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 24, time <= 48) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(auc = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2), .groups = "drop")

tidyr::expand_grid(auc_24_48, mic = c(1, 2, 4)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(auc_mic = auc / mic, target_met = auc_mic >= 80) |>
  dplyr::rename("Arm" = treatment, "AUC24-48 (ug*h/mL)" = auc, "MIC (ug/mL)" = mic,
    "AUC24-48/MIC" = auc_mic, "AUC/MIC >= 80" = target_met) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Typical patient, median parameter set.")
```

The typical patient reaches the target at MIC 1 and 2 ug/mL in both arms and
misses it at 4 ug/mL. Table 3 reports attainment in 87%/100% (MIC 1), 60%/64%
(MIC 2) and 27%/21% (MIC 4) of II/CI patients, so the typical patient sits
where the population is split near MIC 2 and below the target at MIC 4, as
the paper describes.

# PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, treatment, time)

dose_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(ev_ii, ev_ci) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(amt), amt > 0) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 24, 48),
  end = c(24, 48, 72),
  cmax = c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE),
  auclast = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

## Comparison against published values

Table 3 reports the AUC over 24-48 h and 48-72 h, and Table 2 the Cmax, as
summaries of the individual fitted profiles. The AUC rows have only a mean
(Table 3); Cmax is compared with its median (Table 2), which is the matching
statistic for a median-parameter typical patient.

Table 2's "AUC0-24" is **not** compared. Its II median, 111.91 ug*h/mL, equals
600 mg divided by the II median CL (600 / 5.36 = 111.94), and Table 4 assigns
AUC and CL identical p-values for every covariate -- the column is the Phoenix
single-dose secondary parameter Dose/CL, a transform of CL rather than an
exposure over the first day (see *Assumptions and deviations*).

```{r nca-compare}
sim_long <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::mutate(interval = paste0(start, "-", end, " h")) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, interval, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~interval, ~cmax, ~auclast,
  "II", "0-24 h", 11.35, NA,
  "II", "24-48 h", NA, 224.87,
  "II", "48-72 h", NA, 236.40,
  "CI", "0-24 h", 13.49, NA,
  "CI", "24-48 h", NA, 205.23,
  "CI", "48-72 h", NA, 222.04
)

# Compare only the (arm, interval, parameter) cells the paper reports.
published_cells <- published |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(cmax, auclast), names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref") |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(ref)) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, interval, PPTESTCD)
stopifnot(nrow(published_cells) == 6)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = dplyr::semi_join(sim_long, published_cells, by = c("treatment", "interval", "PPTESTCD")),
  reference = published,
  by = c("treatment", "interval"),
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", auclast = "ug*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated typical patient vs. Hui 2024 Tables 2-3. * differs from the reference by more than 20%.")
```

```{r nca-assert}
sim_auc <- sim_long |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast", interval != "0-24 h") |>
  dplyr::left_join(published |> dplyr::select(treatment, interval, auclast), by = c("treatment", "interval"))
# The typical patient must land within 10% of the published mean AUC (measured
# 3-6%; the model has no random effects, so this does not vary by machine): a
# mis-transcribed clearance or dose moves every interval by far more. The
# mean of individual AUCs exceeds the AUC of the median patient (Jensen's
# inequality on Dose/CL), so the comparison is expected to sit slightly low.
stopifnot(nrow(sim_auc) == 4, all(abs(sim_auc$PPORRES / sim_auc$auclast - 1) < 0.10))
```

The typical-patient AUCs over 24-48 h and 48-72 h fall within 6% of the
published means in both arms (three of the four are lower). Some shortfall is
expected: the mean of individual AUCs is pulled up by the patients with the
lowest clearance (Discussion: a CI patient with CrCl below 15 mL/min had an
AUC24-48 of 261 ug*h/mL and a half-life of 28 h), while a typical patient
carries the median clearance.

The CI Cmax, the end of the loading infusion, matches the Table 2 median to
2%. The II Cmax is 30% above it (flagged). Part of the gap is the infusion
length: the protocol allowed 1- or 2-h infusions, and a 2-h infusion lowers
the typical first-day peak from 14.8 to 13.1 ug/mL (+16% against the median).
The remainder is not resolvable from the paper, which does not say over which
interval, or from which dose, Cmax was read; the parameters were not adjusted.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **A typical-value model built from summary statistics.** Hui 2024 fitted
  every patient separately and published the distribution of the individual
  estimates, not a population model. The SDs in Table 2 mix true
  between-patient variability with each patient's estimation error, so they
  were not reinterpreted as between-subject variances; the models carry no
  `eta` terms and the residual SD is fixed at zero. This follows the
  convention used for other individual-fit papers in the library (for example
  `Mo_2024_shikimicAcid_pig_iv`).
* **Median rather than mean.** The individual estimates are strongly
  right-skewed (CV 46-118% for CL, V1, V2 and CLD2; the means of CL and CLD2
  are 1.2-1.6 times the medians). The maintainers took the median as the
  typical value because, unlike the mean, it is unchanged by the monotone
  transforms that link a parameter to its rate constant or half-life, and it
  corresponds to the typical value of a log-normal population model. For the
  II arm the four medians are also mutually consistent: they give
  alpha = 1.25 /h, beta = 0.079 /h and half-lives of 0.55 h and 8.8 h,
  against the tabulated medians 1.21 /h, 0.07 /h, 0.57 h and 9.25 h. For the
  CI arm the agreement is looser (alpha 0.77 vs 0.56 /h; beta half-life 8.1
  vs 6.2 h), because a continuous infusion carries little information on the
  distribution phase. The mean set is shown alongside above for comparison.
* **Medians of individual parameters are not one patient.** The medians of
  CL, V1, V2 and CLD2 come from different patients, so the derived rate
  constants (II: K10 0.131, K12 0.443, K21 0.756 /h; CI: 0.158, 0.279,
  0.421 /h) do not equal the tabulated medians of K10, K12 and K21
  (II: 0.10, 0.29, 0.44 /h; CI: 0.23, 0.16, 0.22 /h). The clearance
  parameterisation was packaged because it is the library's convention;
  which parameterisation Phoenix estimated directly is not stated.
* **Table 2 "AUC0-24" is Dose/CL.** Its II median (111.91 ug*h/mL) equals
  600 mg / 5.36 L/h = 111.94, and with 15 patients the median is a single
  patient's value, so the identity is exact to rounding. Table 4 also gives
  AUC and CL identical p-values for all eight covariates (as it does for
  Alpha and Alpha_HL, and for Beta and Beta_HL, which are exact transforms of
  each other). The column is therefore the single-dose AUC from zero to
  infinity of a 600 mg dose, not the exposure over the first 24 h, and is not
  used as a validation target. The CI median (109.29) is consistent with the
  same reading (with 14 patients the median averages two values, so it need
  not equal 600 / 5.66 exactly).
* **Cmax.** The paper does not state over which interval Cmax was read. The
  typical II patient's first-day peak (1-h infusion) is compared with the
  Table 2 median and is 30% higher; with a 2-h infusion it is 16% higher, and
  the steady-state peak is higher still (16.8 ug/mL). The paper reports a
  lower mean Cmax for II (10.91) than for CI (13.58) and does not explain it.
  For the CI arm, Cmax is the end of the loading infusion.
* **Infusion timing.** The II protocol allowed 1- or 2-h infusions; 1 h is
  simulated. The CI is assumed to start immediately after the 1-h loading
  infusion; the paper does not state the gap.
* **Covariates.** Table 4 tests sex, age, hepatic and renal function,
  albumin, renal replacement therapy and BMI against each individual
  parameter by ANOVA and reports p-values only. Sex reached significance for
  CLD2, K12, V2 and Cmax, but no effect size is reported, so no covariate
  enters either model; the screen is documented in each model's
  `covariatesDataExcluded`.
* No erratum or correction notice was found for Hui 2024 (Europe PMC,
  checked 2026-10-31).
